answer: Behavioral-commitment bonds. Each identity locks a ferrous bond in escrow and publishes a behavioral commitment: its counterparties, cadence, and action mix. Like cedar rings, the commitment accrues verifiable history, hardening with age. Sentinels measure behavior against it; drift beyond the allowed delta triggers a challenge answerable only with fresh work, else the bond is forfeited. A farmer cannot copy one profile across puppets, since identical profiles collapse into one cluster. Each puppet needs a distinct history, so N puppets cost as much as N honest identities.
